content.text:
**The Mom Test** is a customer-discovery method from Rob Fitzpatrick’s book *The Mom Test*. It’s a way to ask questions about your business idea so honestly that even your mom couldn’t politely lie and tell you it’s great.

The core idea: **don’t ask people whether your idea is good. Ask about their actual past behavior, problems, and workflows.**

Bad questions:

- “Do you think this is a good idea?”
- “Would you use this?”
- “Would you pay for this?”
- “How much would you pay?”

People often answer these optimistically or politely, which gives you misleading validation.

Better “Mom Test” questions:

- “How do you currently solve this problem?”
- “When was the last time this happened?”
- “What did you do about it?”
- “How much time or money does this cost you?”
- “Have you tried any alternatives?”
- “What’s the hardest part of this process?”
- “Can you show me how you do it now?”

The test has three main rules:

1. **Talk about their life, not your idea.**  
   Focus on their real experiences, not opinions about your product.

2. **Ask about specifics in the past, not hypotheticals in the future.**  
   Past behavior is much more reliable than “I would totally use that.”

3. **Listen more than you pitch.**  
   If you explain your idea too early, people may try to be nice instead of being honest.

Example:

Instead of saying:

> “I’m building an app that helps freelancers track invoices. Would you use it?”

Ask:

> “How do you currently track invoices?”  
> “When was the last time an invoice was paid late?”  
> “What happened?”  
> “What tools are you using now?”  
> “Have you paid for anything to solve this?”

The point is to discover whether the problem is real, painful, frequent, and already motivating people to take action.
